subject: AI & Agents
title: Voice Assistants and How They Listen
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Voice Assistants and How They Listen.

hook.text: 'Hey Siri' — two words activate a chain of AI systems more complex than most apps.

buildup.text: A small on-device model listens for just the wake word, using almost no power.

discovery.text: Once triggered, your speech is converted to text, parsed for intent, and matched to an action.

twist.text: The assistant doesn't understand meaning. It classifies your request into predefined categories.

climax.text: Modern assistants now use large language models to handle open-ended conversations.

punchline.text: It hears everything after the wake word. Nothing before.

quiz.question: What happens when you say a wake word to a voice assistant?
options: A small model triggers, then speech is converted and classified
The phone starts recording all audio
It sends your voice to a human operator

details.summary: Voice assistants like Siri, Alexa, and Google Assistant use speech recognition and natural language processing to understand commands. They listen for wake words and process requests through cloud AI.
details.whyItMatters: Hundreds of millions of people talk to AI daily. Understanding how voice assistants process speech clarifies their capabilities, limitations, and privacy trade-offs.
takeaways: Voice assistants activate when they detect specific wake words
Speech is processed through cloud-based AI for understanding
Privacy concerns arise from always-listening microphones

faq.question: Are voice assistants always recording everything?
faq.answer: They continuously listen for wake words but only record and transmit audio after activation. However, false triggers do occur, occasionally sending unintended audio to cloud servers.

faq.question: How do voice assistants understand different accents?
faq.answer: Modern speech recognition models are trained on diverse voice samples representing many accents and dialects. Performance has improved dramatically but some accents still receive lower accuracy.
